This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
By consent of both the parties, the appeal is taken up for final disposal though it is slated for admission and heard learned counsel for appellants and respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

This appeal is directed against the judgment and award in MVC No.2683/2016 passed by the learned XXII Additional Small Causes Judge and XX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-24) dated 30.10.2017, whereby, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.11,66,000/- on account of death of one V.Sandeep @ Suresh in the RTA.
3.

The petitioners contended that on 17.02.2016 at about 03.30 pm., the deceased V.Sandeep was walking on a footpath in front of the Swastik Bar at Chikkaballapura and a private bus bearing reg.No.KA-16-B-3563 owned by the respondent No.1 and insured by respondent No.2 came in a negligent manner and dashed against him, resulting in his death.

The petitioners further contended Smt. Vijayamma vs Sri Pasha Jan on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162732256/
2 that they are the parents and sisters of the deceased and were dependents upon the deceased, who was aged about 25 years, earning Rs.15,000/- by working as a Mason.

sentences.text: Therefore, they sought for adequate compensation from the respondents.
4. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and the NC: 2023:KHC:25290 respondent No.1 did not appear, as such, he was placed ex- parte.

5. The respondent No.2-Insurance Company contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law and the petitioners be put to strict proof of the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
They also contended that there was delay in filing the complaint and the liability of the respondent No.2 is subject to validity and effectiveness of the driving license, permit etc.,

There being the violations of the conditions of the policy, the liability be fastened upon respondent No.1.
6.
On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner No.2 was examined as PW.1 and two witnesses were examined as PWs.2 and 3 and Exs.P1 to 17 were marked.
The respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and another witness as RW.2.
Exs.R1 to 3 were marked in evidence.

After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.11,66,000/- under the following heads:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.) Loss of dependency 10,71,000/-
Loss of love and affection 75,000/-
Transportation of body, funeral and 20,000/-
 obsequies expenses

8. Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioners have approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation alleging that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is abysmally low and erroneous.
9. On issuance of notice, respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and the notice to respondent No.1 was dispensed with.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the deceased V.Sandeep was working as a Mason and therefore, there was no valid proof in respect of the income of the deceased and as such, the notional income considered by the Tribunal is justifiable except the quantum of the notional NC: 2023:KHC:25290 income.
In view of the facts and circumstances, the Tribunal had to take notional income that would be applicable for the year 2016.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of the disputes before the Lok-Adalat prescribed a notional income of Rs.9,500/-p.m. for the year 2016.

In umpteen number of decisions, it has been held that the guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act and therefore, the notional income of the deceased is considered at Rs.9,500/- per month.

The deceased was aged 26 years at the time of the accident and therefore,
'loss of dependency' is calculated by considering the 'future prospects' at 40% of same, which comes to Rs.3,800/-.

Therefore, the multiplicand is considered at Rs.13,300/- (Rs.9,500/- + Rs.3,800/-) and the 'loss of dependency' is calculated as Rs.13,300/- X 12 X 17 X 50% = Rs.13,56,600/- by deducting 50% towards personal expenses of the deceased as he was a bachelor.

11. In addition to the above compensation, the petitioners are also entitled for a sum of Rs.48,400/- under the head of 'loss of filial love and affection' and a sum of NC:
2023:KHC:25290 Rs.18,150/- each under the head of 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.
12.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)

Loss of dependency 13,56,600/- Loss of filial love and affection 48,400/-
 Loss of estate and 18,150/-
 Funeral expenses 18,150/-

TOTAL 14,41,300/-
 Less awarded by Tribunal 11,66,000/-
 Enhancement 2,75,300/-
13.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,75,300/-
with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
